### Summary

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
The Python initializer imports torch and the external packages, then the extension.
Import sets float64, one intra-op thread and one inter-op thread.
Order: code map; no independent measured convergence order.
No defining equation: this section maps control flow or data ownership.
:::

The Python initializer imports torch and the external packages, then the extension. The extension exposes row
constants, restart loading and component bindings, while the distribution submodule accepts an external process group.

### Derivation

No separate derivation: this section describes an interface or control-flow path. Numerical operators are derived in
their owning chapters.

### Numerical method

`MeshBlock.forward` releases the Python GIL around the C++ stage call. The Python API therefore reaches the same stage
and exchange ordering described above. Packaging declares build requirements separately from runtime requirements; the
command entry points include combine and inspect tools. Import and binding introduce no independent spatial order or
ghost treatment.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
Python ctests need `SNAPY_TEST_PYTHONPATH` pointing to the package built from the pin; otherwise CMake warns that they
exercise an installed package instead. The import-path check skips with status 125 when no target path is supplied.
Legacy convenience scripts are not taken as evidence for the current binding signature.
:::
